title: The ABC of Mathematical Optimization
scope: Curated A–K course guide and source selection, not a claim of a fully modernized ten-notebook public course

stages.name: Alice
stages.topic: From a story to an objective; symbolic and numerical optimization
stages.reason: The 42-cell MO lecture retains the physical derivation, symbolic versus numeric pi, plots, Pyomo introspection and deliberate late solver installation. The current 10-cell public companion is tested but shorter; use it for execution, not as evidence that the longer narrative is already restored.
goals: Derive the center-of-gravity objective and its feasible interval from the glass and water story.
Distinguish a symbolic stationary point, a feasible candidate, a local minimum and a global minimum.
Compare the same objective across symbolic mathematics and a numerical solver; explain the role of variable bounds.
questions: Why must endpoints be checked when optimizing over a closed interval?
What changes when pi is a floating-point number instead of a symbol?
Which dependencies are needed for symbolic work, plotting, model building and solving, respectively?
stages.public_status: tested companion available; fuller source selected separately

stages.name: Betty
stages.topic: Nonlinear modeling: the cylinder of maximum volume
stages.reason: Betty is the nonlinear maximum-volume cylinder story in the original Optimization Stories family (Colab Notebooks/Betty.ipynb, eight cells). The selected nine-cell MO source calls this same cylinder Francis; that is a historical alias, not this guide's lesson name. It has the same volume objective and surface-area budget. Its installer and unqualified solver calls still need modernization. Betty must not link to Caroline's linear trophy-production notebook.
goals: Formulate radius and height decisions with a surface-area budget.
Separate a nonlinear mathematical expression from a solver interface.
Compare a numerical candidate with analytical reasoning, and account for degenerate starting points.
questions: Why can a starting point at zero be problematic?
Does a local nonlinear solver certify global optimality here?
Can eliminating one variable make the geometry easier to understand?
stages.public_status: source selected; maintained public notebook not yet available

stages.name: Caroline
stages.topic: Linear programming, indexed models, slacks and duals
stages.reason: Caroline is the linear trophy-production story. Use the maintained 79-cell Caroline notebook for its indexed formulations, actual Ipopt/CBC/HiGHS comparison, slacks and duals. The selected 49-cell MO source calls this same LP Betty; retain that source title in provenance, not as the teaching name here. This case is distinct from Betty's nonlinear cylinder.
goals: Translate trophy production into a resource-allocation LP and then an indexed model.
Separate data, variables, objectives and constraint-generation rules.
Explain slacks, binding constraints and dual information, and actually compare solver engines on fresh models.
questions: Which resource limits production and which is left over?
When is it legitimate to interpret a dual value as a marginal value?
Why can two solvers return slightly different numbers without disagreeing on the optimum?
stages.public_status: tested companion available; fuller source selected separately

stages.name: Dina
stages.reason: Keep the MO Dina case and weak/strong formulation derivation. Use the tested Elizabeth notebook for current execution and its real multi-engine comparison. The original 50-facility/100-customer experiment remains a useful scaling extension, not a replacement for comparing LP bounds.
goals: Represent facility opening and customer assignment decisions.
Show why disaggregated linking constraints dominate the aggregate relaxation.
Separate model construction time, solve time, feasible incumbents and certified bounds.
questions: Do stronger inequalities change the integer feasible layouts?
Can the stronger formulation take longer to solve?
What can be concluded when a time limit is reached?
stages.public_status: tested companion available; fuller source selected separately

stages.name: Exploring LAP
stages.topic: Assignment algorithms versus an LP model
stages.reason: Use the 19-cell abstract-model version rather than the earlier 11-cell fragment. It actually compares SciPy assignment with CBC and GLPK. Its 10,000-by-10,000 default would create 100 million variables; preserve the scaling question but choose a bounded default when modernizing. E is the ExploringLAP filename, not an invented character.
goals: Build the bipartite assignment model from a cost matrix.
Explain the integral extreme points of the assignment polytope.
Compare a dedicated assignment algorithm with actual LP solves, including memory and model-building costs.
questions: Why can this assignment model use continuous nonnegative variables?
What changes if additional side constraints are introduced?
What grows quadratically with the number of items?
stages.public_status: source selected; maintained public notebook not yet available

stages.name: Francis
stages.reason: Francis is the purchasing and inventory case in the current ABW materials, also called Hilda in Optimization Stories and Caroline in MO 2020–2021. The selected 55-cell MO source preserves its stepwise development; the maintained private Francis notebook provides the full-case key. The MO notebook titled Francis instead describes Betty's cylinder, so identify the case by its equations and data.
goals: Convert demand for products into demand for materials using a matrix calculation.
Model monthly stock balances, initial and final stock, batches, poles and paired purchasing discounts.
Explain why integer variables, units and delivery/holding-cost timing change the model.
questions: Which quantities must be integer and which could be continuous?
When is inventory highest within the month?
How can a discount for a paired pole and ornament batch be expressed without multiplying decision variables?
stages.public_status: source selected; maintained public notebook not yet available

stages.name: Global and convex optimization
stages.topic: Local optima, convexity and equivalent representations
stages.reason: The 36-cell Global notebook is the coherent lecture, while Untitled8/9 provide supplementary examples. Keep initial-point sensitivity, nonlinear test functions and convex modeling. Correct the blanket complexity statements, replace unrestricted eval and avoid automatic remote submissions.
goals: Use examples to distinguish local minima from global minima.
Check domains and convexity rather than classifying a problem solely by its syntax.
Recognize when a reformulation exposes convex structure to a solver.
questions: Can an equivalent expression be easier for a modeling system to recognize?
What assumptions are required before a local optimum is also global?
Why is a blanket claim about the complexity of all global optimization misleading?
stages.public_status: source selected; maintained public notebook not yet available

stages.name: Holistic convex optimization
stages.topic: Subgradient methods, Newton steps and Lagrange duality
stages.reason: Choose the full 66-cell lecture, not the 34-cell Week 3 draft. It connects symbolic derivatives to strategies, Newton steps, projection and abstract Pyomo Lagrangian subproblems, including alternative duals of the same problem. It explicitly teaches delayed imports and avoiding copy-and-paste.
goals: Implement and inspect progress and projection strategies.
Distinguish primal variables, multipliers, relaxed subproblem solutions and subgradients.
Connect multiplier domains and update signs to the chosen primal/dual convention.
questions: Does a small change in successive iterates prove optimality?
When must multipliers be projected onto a nonnegative or nonpositive domain?
Which code should remain visible in the algorithm lesson and which should later applications import?
stages.public_status: source selected; maintained public notebook not yet available

stages.name: Ignacio
stages.topic: Stochastic programming and uncertain nutrient coefficients
stages.reason: Choose the 50-cell lecture over the 48-cell checkpoint. It links repeated blending solves, simulations, averages and extremes with symbolic value-function analysis and optional animations. Preserve the distinction between optimizing averaged inputs and averaging optimized outcomes.
goals: Model uncertain calcium/protein coefficients and evaluate the resulting decisions.
Separate a fixed decision chosen before uncertainty from an adaptive decision chosen after observing it.
Compare numerical repeated solves with the derived value function on common observations.
questions: Are decisions made before or after the nutrient coefficients are observed?
Why need the optimum at average data differ from the average of optima?
How should seed, sample size and evaluation scenarios be controlled in a comparison?
stages.source_relative: Lectures/Notebooks for lectures/Ignacio blends with uncertain data.ipynb
stages.public_status: source selected; maintained public notebook not yet available

stages.name: Joan and Karin
stages.topic: From empirical uncertainty to robust and conic optimization
stages.reason: Choose the 58-cell lecture, not the 56-cell Copy or 51-cell Week 5 predecessor. J and K share one notebook: Joan analyzes observations; Karin builds box, budget/cardinality and ball uncertainty models, then continuous and mixed-integer conic versions. Keep the actual Ipopt/Gurobi/CPLEX/Xpress roles and later introductions.
goals: Explain how observations motivate an uncertainty set without treating that set as a probability distribution.
Derive and compare box, budgeted and ball-uncertainty counterparts.
Keep the nonnegative cone-side condition when squaring a norm inequality; distinguish continuous conic from mixed-integer conic solving.
questions: What conservatism is introduced by a box uncertainty set?
What does the uncertainty budget control?
Why does dropping the sign restriction when squaring a cone change the feasible set?
stages.source_relative: Lectures/Notebooks for lectures/Joan and Karin's story on week 5.ipynb
stages.public_status: source selected; maintained public notebook not yet available

naming_policy: Curated teaching names: Alice (stable vase), Betty (nonlinear cylinder), Caroline (linear trophies), Francis (purchasing/inventory). Historical MO titles are recorded separately; this is not a single historical alphabet.
